acceptance_criteria.source_text: All eight mandatory files exist, are non-empty, and use the exact required paths. index.html loads only local relative assets and starts the game through src/main.js.
The game loads locally in a modern browser without dependencies, external network requests, uncaught page exceptions, or material console errors.

The game uses a full-window or prominently sized Canvas arena representing a world larger than the viewport. A camera follows the player through that world rather than keeping all gameplay fixed to one small screen.
Player steering is continuous and pointer-driven. Moving the mouse or pointer changes the serpent's heading smoothly; gameplay must not be limited to four grid directions.
The player is visibly represented as a continuous multi-segment serpent with a head, body, and length. The body follows the head rather than behaving like a single dot or square.
Collectible pellets exist throughout the arena. Collecting pellets increases the player's visible length or mass and updates an on-screen score or length value.

acceptance_criteria.source_text: The player can boost using a documented keyboard or pointer control. Boosting visibly increases speed and has a bounded gameplay cost such as gradual length or mass reduction.
Collision and lifecycle behavior exist. A serpent can die, death can release pellets or equivalent collectible mass, and the player can respawn or restart without reloading the page.

At least 12 autonomous bot serpents exist simultaneously. They move through the arena, seek or encounter pellets, remain bounded by the game world, and participate in the same growth or competition system.
A visible leaderboard displays the player and bots using live game state and updates during play.

The game has explicit lifecycle states covering running, paused, dead, and respawning or restarted behavior. Pause/resume and restart controls are documented and must not create duplicate animation loops.
The visible interface includes the game title, score or length, leaderboard, concise controls, and clear feedback for death, pause, and restart.

The page exposes a read-only runtime debug interface: window.__NEON__.snapshot() snapshot() must be a zero-argument function returning JSON-serializable data with exactly these eight top-level fields: phase: string player: object containing x, y, length, alive, and boosting botCount: number pelletCount: number leaderboard: array respawnCount: number loopCount: number debugVisible: boolean The debug interface must expose observations only. It must not provide mutation, cheating, success-forcing, file, shell, or network capabilities. Loading index.html with ?debug=1 must display a bounded debug overlay based on the same runtime state. loopCount must increase while the one canonical animation loop is running and must not reveal duplicate loops after pause, resume, death, respawn, or restart.

The visual presentation must be polished and coherent: neon arena styling, readable HUD, clearly distinguishable player, bots, pellets, and effects, without obvious broken layout or placeholder presentation.
Pointer steering, camera movement, body following, boosting, pause, death, respawn, and restart must feel reasonably smooth and responsive during direct human observation.
